The question involves a 22-year-old female experiencing symptoms such as facial flushing, nausea, tachycardia, dyspnea, headache, and abdominal cramps after consuming alcohol while being treated with metronidazole. Metronidazole is known to cause a disulfiram-like reaction. 

Disulfiram-like reactions are characterized by the build-up of acetaldehyde when alcohol is consumed because both disulfiram and metronidazole inhibit the enzyme acetaldehyde dehydrogenase. This enzyme is responsible for converting acetaldehyde (a metabolite of ethanol) into acetic acid. Inhibiting this enzyme leads to elevated levels of acetaldehyde, which results in the symptoms described.

E. Amylase - Unrelated to this mechanism.
